row1.revenue: Amazon (AMZN) tops the revenue list with $716.9 B, outpacing Walmart (WMT) by roughly $3.7 B. The gap between the top two is the largest, while the rest of the group falls 150 B+ below Amazon.

row1.total_assets: JPMorgan Chase leads total assets with $4.4 trillion, far ahead of Bank of America’s $3.4 trillion. The gap between the top two banks is $1.0 trillion, while the next tier of tech giants trails by more than $1.5 trillion.
row1.total_equity: Microsoft (MSFT) leads Total Equity at $442.4 B, outpacing Alphabet (GOOGL) by roughly $27 B. The gap narrows further to Amazon (AMZN) at $411.1 B, leaving JPMorgan Chase (JPM) and Bank of America (BAC) well behind the top tier.
row1.total_liabilities: JPMorgan Chase leads Total Liabilities at $4.1 trillion, far ahead of Bank of America’s $3.1 trillion and a steep drop to Amazon’s $407 billion, showing a $3.0 trillion gap between the top two banks and the tech sector.
row1.cash_and_equivalents: JPMorgan Chase leads the pack with $343.3 B in cash and equivalents, a full $104 B more than Bank of America’s $239.3 B, underscoring its dominant liquidity position. Amazon, Apple, and Meta trail far behind, each holding less than $90 B.
row1.gross_profit: Amazon leads gross profit with $360.5B, outpacing Alphabet by $120.2B and Microsoft by $135.0B, highlighting a significant gap at the top of the list. The next tier-Apple, Walmart, and Microsoft-clusters within $30B of each other, showing tighter competition below Amazon.
row1.operating_income_ebit: Microsoft leads with an operating income of $155.2 B, outpacing Apple by $22.1 B and NVIDIA by $24.8 B, while Alphabet trails just $1.4 B behind NVIDIA. The gap between the top two is the largest, underscoring Microsoft’s dominant profitability in the tech sector.
